sentences.text: As worded the premise is false: fiscal 2026 revenue grew 65.5%, short of the doubling line by $45.06B, so the claim fails on the very year it names.

The doubling the thesis describes belongs to FY2024 (+125.9%) and FY2025 (+114.2%); fiscal 2026 is the year growth slowed, by 48.7 percentage points, so the claim reads the trend backwards for that year.
The implications agree with the miss rather than hiding a doubling elsewhere: gross profit and operating cash flow also fell short of doubling, and receivables outgrew revenue.
The claim still points at something real on a different basis: the newest quarter, Q2 FY2027, grew 105.9% on a year earlier, so doubling shows up after the fiscal year ended, not within it.

For the buy decision, the step from growth to price is what matters: at the 2026-09-30 price the reverse DCF needs 13.4% a year for 10 years, a pace 0 of 40 comparably sized ten-year spans reached, and it leans most on the 65.2% operating margin held every year.
The record cannot say whether the quarter's doubling persists, and its quality carries a caveat: receivable days rose to 59.6 from 54.1 as receivables grew faster than revenue.
The newest quarter did double on a year earlier, so a reader taking the claim as 'revenue is doubling' rather than 'fiscal 2026 doubled' has current support.
Billings ahead of delivery outpaced recognized revenue, with deferred revenue up 215.1% against revenue up 105.9%, which is consistent with demand not yet booked.
Even the 65.5% fiscal-year pace ranks 6 of 63 among SIC 3674 filers with revenue of at least $100.0M, against a class median of 13.0%.

Doubling at this scale has no precedent in the record: among other filers with revenue of at least $100.00B it held in 0 of 366 company-years, and among SIC 3674 filers it held in 15 of 1045, with only 3 of 12 readable cases holding again a year later.
Growth rests on one segment: Data Center contributed 60.2 percentage points of the 65.5% fiscal 2026 growth, so any doubling depends on that single line.
Receivables grew 126.8% against revenue's 105.9% in the newest quarter, so part of the reported doubling has not yet turned into cash.
Whether the decision should weigh the fiscal-year basis, where the claim fails, or the newest quarter, where revenue did double.
Whether doubling is even needed: the price at 2026-09-30 asks for 13.4% a year, so the decision turns more on whether the 65.2% operating margin holds than on whether growth doubles.
Whether the receivables build reverses into cash or keeps widening relative to revenue.

conditions.text: A later filing showing the trailing operating margin below the 65.2% the reverse DCF assumes would weaken the case that growth alone carries the price.
A later quarter with revenue below the $96.22B of Q2 FY2027 would show the quarterly doubling has not carried forward.
Deferred revenue falling below the $6.41B of Q2 FY2027 would remove the sign of billings running ahead of revenue.
